paths.title: Testing Strategy & Verification
paths.description: Use layered automated and manual evidence to prove AI-generated behavior rather than trusting compilation or model confidence.

lessons.title: Test behavior, not implementation trivia
lessons.principle: Tests should protect meaningful outcomes while allowing internal refactoring.
lessons.practice: Assert public behavior, state transitions, contracts, and important side effects.

lessons.title: Build a testing pyramid pragmatically
lessons.principle: Fast tests support iteration; broader tests protect integration.
lessons.practice: Use many focused unit tests, boundary integration tests, and a smaller set of critical end-to-end journeys.

lessons.title: Write tests from acceptance criteria
lessons.principle: Requirements are strongest when they become executable evidence.
lessons.practice: Map each important acceptance scenario to one or more automated or explicit manual checks.

lessons.title: Test negative cases
lessons.principle: Happy-path tests miss many production defects.
lessons.practice: Cover invalid input, permissions, missing resources, timeouts, conflicts, and dependency failures.

lessons.title: Test boundaries
lessons.principle: Off-by-one and threshold defects are common in generated code.
lessons.practice: Exercise empty, minimum, maximum, just-inside, and just-outside values.

lessons.title: Test authorization separately
lessons.principle: A feature can work functionally while exposing data.
lessons.practice: Verify each role against allowed and forbidden resources and actions.

lessons.title: Test persistence behavior
lessons.principle: Mocks can hide schema, transaction, and query problems.
lessons.practice: Use integration tests against a representative database for critical data flows.

lessons.title: Test external adapters
lessons.principle: Third-party contracts fail in unusual ways.
lessons.practice: Simulate success, retryable errors, permanent errors, slow responses, malformed payloads, and duplicate events.

lessons.title: Use deterministic fixtures
lessons.principle: Flaky randomness erodes confidence.
lessons.practice: Control clocks, seeds, identifiers, external calls, and test data.

lessons.title: Avoid over-mocking
lessons.principle: Mocks that duplicate implementation assumptions can make broken systems appear green.
lessons.practice: Mock true external boundaries and exercise real internal collaboration where practical.

lessons.title: Use property-based tests where useful
lessons.principle: Some rules span many possible inputs.
lessons.practice: Generate diverse inputs for parsers, serializers, invariants, and mathematical properties.

lessons.title: Use snapshot tests selectively
lessons.principle: Large snapshots can approve accidental changes blindly.
lessons.practice: Keep snapshots focused and review diffs rather than updating them reflexively.

lessons.title: Test migrations
lessons.principle: Schema code should be verified like application code.
lessons.practice: Apply migrations from realistic prior states and test mixed-version compatibility where relevant.

lessons.title: Test concurrency
lessons.principle: Single-threaded tests cannot reveal all race conditions.
lessons.practice: Exercise duplicate submissions, conflicting edits, locking, and idempotency.

lessons.title: Test performance budgets
lessons.principle: Functionally correct code can still fail at scale.
lessons.practice: Add benchmarks or load checks for hot paths with meaningful thresholds.

lessons.title: Test accessibility
lessons.principle: Automated checks catch only part of accessibility.
lessons.practice: Combine automated scanning with keyboard, focus, semantics, and screen-reader checks.

lessons.title: Use visual regression where valuable
lessons.principle: UI refactors can change appearance without DOM failures.
lessons.practice: Capture stable critical components or flows and review meaningful visual differences.

lessons.title: Run focused checks during iteration
lessons.principle: Fast feedback keeps the agent aligned.
lessons.practice: Run the smallest relevant test set after each coherent change before full-suite validation.

lessons.title: Run the full gate before merge
lessons.principle: Local focused success does not prove repository-wide compatibility.
lessons.practice: Execute required lint, types, tests, build, security, and integration checks on the final head.

lessons.title: Treat failing tests as evidence
lessons.principle: A failing test is information about either code or an outdated requirement.
lessons.practice: Investigate the reason before changing production code or weakening the assertion.

paths.title: Debugging & Root-Cause Analysis
paths.description: Diagnose defects with evidence, reproducibility, and causal reasoning instead of prompting the model to make random patches.

lessons.title: Reproduce before fixing
lessons.principle: A reliable reproduction defines the actual problem.
lessons.practice: Capture exact inputs, environment, steps, expected behavior, and observed behavior.

lessons.title: Reduce the failing case
lessons.principle: Smaller reproductions reveal which variables matter.
lessons.practice: Remove unrelated data, components, or steps while preserving the failure.

lessons.title: Read the error literally
lessons.principle: Stack traces and diagnostics often identify the failing boundary.
lessons.practice: Start from the first relevant error and trace data and control flow around it.

lessons.title: Distinguish symptom from cause
lessons.principle: Visible failures may originate far upstream.
lessons.practice: Ask what invariant became false first rather than patching the last line that crashed.

lessons.title: Compare working and failing states
lessons.principle: Differences narrow the search space.
lessons.practice: Compare environment, inputs, versions, flags, permissions, and recent commits.

lessons.title: Use logs with correlation
lessons.principle: Distributed failures need a thread across components.
lessons.practice: Preserve request, job, or user-safe correlation identifiers through logs and traces.

lessons.title: Inspect actual runtime values
lessons.principle: Model reasoning about hypothetical values is weaker than evidence.
lessons.practice: Use debugger, structured logs, assertions, or temporary instrumentation to inspect state.

lessons.title: Bisect regressions
lessons.principle: When a bug appeared after a known good version, history is evidence.
lessons.practice: Use commit bisection or controlled rollback to find the first bad change.

lessons.title: Check environmental drift
lessons.principle: Builds can fail because runtime and local assumptions differ.
lessons.practice: Compare environment variables, versions, platform, filesystem, network, and data state.

lessons.title: Check race conditions
lessons.principle: Intermittent failures often depend on timing.
lessons.practice: Look for shared mutable state, missing awaits, duplicate events, stale reads, and unsafe retries.

lessons.title: Check caches
lessons.principle: Stale state can make new code appear broken.
lessons.practice: Identify browser, CDN, application, build, database, and service-worker caches in the path.

lessons.title: Check serialization boundaries
lessons.principle: Data can change shape across JSON, dates, numbers, and nullable fields.
lessons.practice: Inspect encoded and decoded representations at each boundary.

lessons.title: Check permissions and identity
lessons.principle: Many apparent not-found or server errors are authorization problems.
lessons.practice: Inspect the authenticated identity, scopes, ownership, and policy decisions.

lessons.title: Check database state
lessons.principle: Schema and data invariants may differ from assumptions.
lessons.practice: Inspect migrations, constraints, representative rows, locks, and query plans.

lessons.title: Avoid shotgun fixes
lessons.principle: Changing many plausible causes at once destroys diagnostic information.
lessons.practice: Test one hypothesis at a time or isolate changes so cause remains attributable.

lessons.title: Use temporary assertions
lessons.principle: Assertions can expose the first violated invariant closer to its source.
lessons.practice: Add targeted checks during investigation and remove or formalize them after the fix.

lessons.title: Turn the bug into a test
lessons.principle: A regression test prevents recurrence and proves the fix addresses the observed case.
lessons.practice: Write the failing test before or alongside the correction when feasible.

lessons.title: Validate adjacent behavior
lessons.principle: A narrow bug fix can break neighboring cases.
lessons.practice: Test both the reproduction and nearby valid scenarios.

lessons.title: Remove diagnostic noise
lessons.principle: Temporary logs and flags can leak data or clutter production.
lessons.practice: Clean up investigation artifacts before merge unless they provide durable observability.

lessons.title: Write the root cause
lessons.principle: A concise causal explanation improves future prevention.
lessons.practice: Document trigger, violated assumption, why existing checks missed it, fix, and prevention.

git bisect bad HEAD
